daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

A panel discussion at Universitas Gadjah Mada featuring government officials Budiman Sudjatmiko, Nusron Wahid, and Deputy Agriculture Minister Sudaryono descended into chaos when students disrupted the event, with SEMA UGM stating the officials were not fit to speak about Pancasila. The Deputy Agriculture Minister denied fleeing the scene and claimed he was struck, while Nusron said he invited Islamic chanting during the commotion and Budiman complained conditions were not conducive for discussion.

  • Vice President Gibran received student representatives who issued a five-day ultimatum to the government, with Gibran stating he appreciated their expression of aspirations.
  • Former President Megawati defended student demonstrations at Bundaran HI, telling protesters not to be afraid.
  • Gelora party chairman commented on limiting party leadership terms, saying regeneration is inevitable.
  • PKS politician Anis Matta said there is no reason to maintain the parliamentary threshold.
  • Former Coordinating Minister Mahfud MD criticized the National Police Law for ignoring reform commission recommendations, suggesting some are afraid.
  • The Home Affairs Minister urged local governments to expand home renovation support through regional budgets while inspecting housing subsidy recipients in West Jakarta.
  • PBNU announced 1 Muharram falls on Wednesday 17 June 2026, differing from the government's determination.

Foreign Policy & Defence

President Prabowo spoke by telephone with Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas, during which Prabowo reaffirmed Indonesia's support for Palestine and told Abbas that a two-state solution is the only path to peace. Indonesia's Foreign Ministry welcomed the US-Iran peace agreement and urged immediate de-escalation in the Middle East.

  • German President Steinmeier emphasized the Germany-Indonesia partnership amid global conflicts, with Germany viewing Indonesia as a key pillar of stability in ASEAN.
  • Indonesia and Germany pushed for stronger economic partnership and investment, with Indonesia set to host the second Indonesia-Germany Joint Economic and Investment Committee meeting this year.
  • Indonesia and Qatar strengthened their strategic partnership through political consultations, with Qatar backing Indonesia's growth agenda with a $4 billion commitment.
  • Indonesia and Albania are preparing an MoU on cooperation for Indonesian migrant worker placement.
  • The Indonesian government is handling allegations of violence against an Indonesian migrant worker in Johor, Malaysia, with the Foreign Ministry urged to ensure strict punishment for the perpetrator.
  • A defence minister stated Indonesia's future depends on strong maritime defence capabilities.

Other

The National Food Security Agency (BGN) prohibited its employees from operating free meal kitchens (MBG), with BGN stating the budget still comes from education and health allocations and opening the possibility that high school students from wealthy families may not receive free meals. BGN also addressed the fate of 21,000 electric motorcycles worth Rp 1 trillion.

  • Investment Coordinating Board Minister Purbaya will fly to China on Tuesday to pursue investors and was surprised that assets of fugitive Eddy Tansil could still be recovered.
  • Foreign investors rushed into Indonesian stocks following a recent market sell-off, with Danantara CEO acknowledging foreign investors were initially hesitant about Indonesia but are now positive.
  • US investors led the rush for Danantara's debut $1.5 billion global bond issuance.
  • Indonesia regained access to the EU aquaculture market and kicked off the 2026 economic census.
  • A minister proposed raising the subsidized diesel quota for 2027, while state railway operator prepares full transition to B50 biodiesel fuel.
